excerpt: If you’re switching to Mac, start here to make it a smooth transition. Learn how to find your way around the Mac, how to transfer your files from your PC, and more.
Your Mac works seamlessly with all your other Apple devices. View and control your iPhone right from your Mac desktop, copy and paste between devices, and more.
Your Mac includes built-in tools to protect your important information—from password management to private browsing and beyond.
Developers will love macOS 27, too.
a new slider lets you easily customize how Liquid Glass looks, from ultraclear to fully tinted.
Create unique, high-quality images for any project in just about any style, including photorealistic.
Automate daily tasks with a simple description. Just describe what you need and Shortcuts connects actions across multiple apps to get it done.
Now your tabs can be automatically grouped into topics, so related pages are easier to find on your Mac.
The Passwords app alerts you to weak or compromised passwords and can update them on your behalf without the hassle.

Confirmed root login with empty password unlocks preferences pane on High Sierra 10.13.1; also works from login screen with user switching enabled, described as a full authentication bypass, not just a UI bug.
Root bug could be exploited remotely via Remote Desktop/Remote Management, but only after gaining physical access once first.
Bug did not work on cold boot with FileVault enabled, and sudo su root with empty password also failed.
Tested and confirmed the root bug was NOT present in Sierra (10.12.6), suggesting it was newly introduced in High Sierra.

Longtime Mac user: window resizing has 'always sucked' - historically only the lower-right corner could resize windows, and even after Apple added edge resizing, there's no visible frame or target zone, unlike other OSes.
In Tahoe, trying to resize a window near the corner can accidentally click through to and activate the window behind it, hiding the one being resized.
Tahoe is a macOS misstep on par with Windows 8 or Vista; 'I don't recommend others upgrade. I wish I didn't.'

After a week with Tahoe, one user left it in their bag: 'Window operations are painful and it feels like a bad try at a tablet os without a stylus or touch screen.' Switched primary use to a Linux laptop.
User finds resizing actually easier in Tahoe because the cursor now splits into two dramatic triangles when in the resize zone, versus the subtler pre-Tahoe cursor.
Third-party tools like Moom and Moves are used as workarounds to resize windows without needing to grab a specific corner, calling them 'life changing small things.'

macOS sends hashes of every opened executable to Apple's servers via trustd/syspolicyd; when ocsp.apple.com went down, the entire OS ground to a halt system-wide, even on older Mojave/Catalina machines not running Big Sur.
Workaround: add '0.0.0.0 ocsp.apple.com' to /etc/hosts and flush DNS cache to restore ability to launch apps.

User's MacBook was 'basically unusable' during the OCSP outage: 'Your services hanging should never prevent my device from running things locally. This is seriously making me reconsider my next computer purchase.'
Concern raised that this design means Apple (and by extension law enforcement) can surveil every app launch via the certificate check hash - 'seems so much scarier than any malware.'
pbcopy/pbpaste praised repeatedly as extremely useful command-line clipboard tools; one user pipes JSON through 'pbpaste | jq | pbcopy' to quickly reformat clipboard contents.
qlmanage recommended as a handy way to convert SVG to PNG without installing extra software: 'qlmanage -t -s 1000x1000 -o file.png file.svg'.
hidutil is useful for remapping keyboard keys (e.g., CapsLock) without third-party software, using JSON property mapping commands.
Catalina performs synchronous network calls (notarization/Gatekeeper checks) before executing any new binary, even simple one-line shell scripts, causing noticeable launch delays.
On a spotty train WiFi connection, 'go build' would unpredictably take up to 30 seconds instead of 100ms, later traced to notarization checks blocking on network connectivity.

After disabling iCloud, Siri, location, and background network access, user still finds 'it phones home constantly even with all of the services disabled/opted out' - calling it a privacy mess, not just a performance one.
